cards.explanation: The answer is False. Jeremiah says he has "…neither lent nor borrowed…" and still everyone curses him. (Jeremiah 15:10) No loan in the picture, and the cursing comes anyway. I think that's what stings.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says, "surely I will intercede with your enemy in your time of trouble, in your time of distress." (Jeremiah 15:11) He names the trouble and the distress right there, out loud. Then He promises to step in.

The answer is "In a land you do not know." The LORD says He will enslave them to their enemies "…in a land you do not know…" (Jeremiah 15:14) That's the place He names for it. It's a heavy line, friends, and it's okay to say so.

The answer is that Jeremiah asks the LORD to avenge him against his persecutors. He prays, "Avenge me against my persecutors." (Jeremiah 15:15) He doesn't dress it up or soften it. I think that's part of why this passage feels so honest.

The answer is False. Jeremiah says, "Know that I endure reproach for Your honor." (Jeremiah 15:15) He's speaking to the LORD, so "Your honor" means the LORD's. It's not a prayer about his own reputation.
The answer is that he ate them, friends. Jeremiah says, "Your words were found, and I ate them." (Jeremiah 15:16) Words taken in, not set aside. I think he treats them like something he needed.

The answer is False. Jeremiah says, "Your words became my joy and my heart’s delight." (Jeremiah 15:16) There's no heavy burden in that line. Joy and delight are what he names, even in a chapter full of trouble.

The answer is the band of revelers. Jeremiah says, "I never sat with the band of revelers, nor did I celebrate with them." (Jeremiah 15:17) The revelers are the group he names, friends. He says he didn't sit with them or celebrate with them.

The answer is "alone." Jeremiah says, "Because Your hand was on me, I sat alone…" (Jeremiah 15:17) He ties it to the LORD's hand on him. Sitting alone sounds quiet, but I think it was a heavy kind of quiet.

The answer is a mirage, bakers. Jeremiah tells the LORD, "You have indeed become like a mirage to me…" (Jeremiah 15:18) Notice he says "like." He's describing how it feels to him, and he says it right to the LORD.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "If you return, I will restore you; you will stand in My presence." (Jeremiah 15:19) Restore and stand in His presence are both right there in one promise. After all that complaining, friends, that's a lot of welcome.

The answer is the LORD's spokesman. The LORD says, "…if you speak words that are noble instead of worthless, you will be My spokesman." (Jeremiah 15:19) A spokesman speaks for Someone else. Good words go with that job.

The answer is True, bakers. The LORD says, "It is they who must turn to you, but you must not turn to them." (Jeremiah 15:19) The direction matters here. Jeremiah isn't supposed to bend toward the people.

The answer is bronze, friends. The LORD says, "Then I will make you a wall to this people, a fortified wall of bronze…" (Jeremiah 15:20) A wall of bronze is a lot sturdier than anything my cookie sheets could manage. It's the LORD's promise of strength.
The answer is False. The LORD says, "they will fight against you but will not overcome you…" (Jeremiah 15:20) He says they will fight against Jeremiah. The promise is that they will not overcome him.

The answer is that the LORD is with him to save him. The LORD says, "…for I am with you to save and deliver you…" (Jeremiah 15:20) That's the reason, friends, and the LORD gives it Himself. The wall holds because He is with Jeremiah.

The answer is that the LORD will rescue him from their hands, bakers. The LORD says, "I will deliver you from the hand of the wicked and redeem you from the grasp of the ruthless." (Jeremiah 15:21) Deliver and redeem both mean rescue. The chapter ends on a promise.
